title: Gilbert known-key · 7-round differential core

target.description: 9-round AES with independent public round keys; initial whitening and omitted final MixColumns per Section2. Multiple-differential core and Gilbert boundary extension.

setting.key_relation: Public independently chosen whitening and round keys; all are known to the shortcut player.
setting.key_population: Public independently selected 128-bit whitening and round keys
setting.plaintext_model: n distinct unordered pair-of-pairs. After one input round and one inverse output round, each tuple has a difference in some D_j and M_l respectively; the existential witness offsets are shared across all tuples.
assumptions: Gilbert known-key relation; verifier searches for existential boundary offsets, not the unknown original master key. No AES key-schedule constraint is imposed on the existential boundary offsets. Case2: the generic reference counts both permutation/inverse queries and the extra computation needed to identify satisfying tuples; the shortcut budget includes tuple generation and verifier work.
The source does not prove that the proposed generic-player strategy is optimal; Section12 leaves that question open.
setting.reference_model: Gilbert known-key relation; verifier searches for existential boundary offsets, not the unknown original master key. No AES key-schedule constraint is imposed on the existential boundary offsets. Case2: the generic reference counts both permutation/inverse queries and the extra computation needed to identify satisfying tuples; the shortcut budget includes tuple generation and verifier work.

time.note: Tuple-generation plus verifier costs under the same n. Source Table2 verifier normalization is retained.

data.note: Output witnesses generated by the public-cipher algorithm; not secret-key data queries.

memory.note: Table1/Table2 memory exponent; no uniform entry-width conversion is asserted.

preprocessing.note: Rebound/key-filter setup is retained within the source total estimate; no separate reusable setup amount is stated.

success.description: The source states construction costs and qualitative success or expected tuple generation, without a numerical fixed-budget shortcut-player success law.

review.scope: PDF p.11 Table2; pp.51–52 AppendixE.3.1. Primary shortcut output event checked separately from generic-player probabilities.

evidence.interpretation: Defining primary-text costs, output event and conditions checked together.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.4–5 Table1; p.21 Section5 key-schedule versus independent witnesses.
evidence.interpretation: Later journal checked for contribution overlap: its Table1 does not list the preprint nine-round or refined scheduled-key entries. This does not establish withdrawal or invalidate the preprint claim. Exact publication identity and later treatment remain an evidence task.

limitations: The result is a known-key witness construction, not secret-key recovery.
The original source model and generic-reference cost case are retained.
